text:
A: Alright? Darren. Can you hear me?
B: Yes, hello. I'm Abena. Herne Hill, in London.
A: Bridgwater, Somerset. Nice to meet you.
B: You too. I noticed the starlings on your calendar. Is that local to you?
A: Yeah, Ham Wall, on the Levels. That one's bought, but I photograph them myself. Got into photography about five years ago, saved up for a second-hand Fuji. The Levels, the murmurations, Hinkley from a distance at dusk.
B: Hinkley? The power station?
A: Yeah, the construction. Sounds daft, but at dusk, with the cranes all lit up across the water, it's sort of beautiful. Industrial, you know? People think Bridgwater's just a place you drive past, but there's stuff there.
B: No, it doesn't sound daft at all. There's a long tradition of that, painting factories and industry. The light on something ugly can be the most interesting thing.
A: That's it, that's exactly it. The light on something ugly. I'll be using that.
B: (laughs) Please do. Do you show them anywhere?
A: Local Facebook group mostly. One of the murmurations got a couple of hundred likes. Others, not so much. Bit gutting when you've stood out there two hours.
B: Erm, I think likes are a strange way to judge it. Some of the best work I've seen gets very little attention. Have you thought about printing them?
A: Not really. Wouldn't know where to start.
B: A local library or café will often hang work. It's sort of how many people start.
A: Huh. Might look into that. What do you do, then?
B: Interior design, part-time, for a studio in Dulwich.
A: Oh, nice. I'm tiling our downstairs loo at the moment, myself. We own the place, ex-council semi, so I do all the DIY. Laminate, shelves, the lot.
B: Well done. Tiling is harder than people think. What tiles?
A: Plain white, metro ones. Cheap, Wickes. Kerry wanted grey.
B: White metro is safe. Have you thought about a coloured grout? A dark one with white tiles can look very smart, and it hides the dirt in a toilet.
A: Dark grout. Never even thought of that. Hides the dirt, that's a selling point with an eight-year-old in the house.
B: (laughs) Exactly. Practical and pretty.
A: So you do posh houses, then?
B: Some. Period houses mostly, Victorian. I've done one for someone quite well known, but I'm not allowed to say.
A: Go on.
B: No. (laughs) But honestly, the small jobs are often more satisfying. Someone who's saved up for one room.
A: Fair enough. I'm a machine operator, packaging, at a food plant. Shifts.
B: That must take real concentration.
A: It does, yeah. Most people don't get that. Changeovers, fault codes —
